description: Standard US supermarket department ordering, perimeter-first. Used to sort the shopping list the way people actually walk a store. Store hints are for Northeast Ohio (Summit County) chains.

aisles.name: Produce
aisles.hint: Walk the outer wall first. Buy hardy vegetables (carrots, cabbage, squash) for late-week meals and delicate greens for early-week meals.

aisles.name: Bakery & Bread
aisles.hint: Look for 'whole grain' as the first ingredient and under 150 mg sodium per slice.

aisles.name: Deli & Prepared
aisles.hint: Deli meats are a top-5 sodium source in the American diet. Buy roasted turkey breast sliced fresh instead of pre-packaged when you can.

aisles.name: Meat & Seafood
aisles.hint: Only needed for the omnivore add-ons. Ask the counter to portion and vacuum-seal in meal-size packs so you can freeze the rest.

aisles.name: Dairy & Eggs
aisles.hint: Plain Greek yogurt does the work of sour cream, mayo, and cream in most of these recipes.

aisles.name: Frozen
aisles.hint: Frozen vegetables are picked and frozen at peak ripeness; nutritionally they match or beat out-of-season fresh in Ohio in January.

aisles.name: Canned & Jarred
aisles.hint: Choose 'no salt added' beans and tomatoes. Rinsing regular canned beans in a colander removes roughly 40% of their sodium.

aisles.name: Pasta, Rice & Grains
aisles.hint: Dry lentils, farro, and brown rice are the cheapest calories in the store and the highest fiber.

aisles.name: Nuts, Seeds & Dried Fruit
aisles.hint: Buy raw and unsalted; toast them yourself in a dry skillet for 3 minutes. Store nuts in the freezer so they never go rancid.

aisles.name: Baking
aisles.hint: Flour, cornstarch, cocoa, baking powder — restock quarterly, not weekly.

aisles.name: Condiments & Sauces
aisles.hint: Dijon, vinegars, and a good hot sauce carry more flavor per milligram of sodium than anything else in the store.

aisles.name: Oils & Vinegars
aisles.hint: One good extra-virgin olive oil in a dark bottle is worth more than three mediocre oils.

aisles.name: Spices & Seasoning
aisles.hint: Spices are the whole heart-healthy trick: they replace salt. Replace ground spices yearly — old spices are why 'healthy' food tastes flat.

aisles.name: International
aisles.hint: Miso, gochujang, curry paste, and tahini live here and each one turns a plain pot of vegetables into dinner.

heinens-hudson.name: Heinen's
heinens-hudson.note: Produce and the cheese counter at the front, butcher and seafood along the back wall. Bulk grains and nuts are worth using for lentils and farro.

giant-eagle.name: Giant Eagle
giant-eagle.note: Larger center store; bring the list grouped by aisle or you will walk the whole thing twice.

kroger.name: Kroger
kroger.note: Produce at the entrance, then the perimeter for meat, seafood and dairy. The natural-foods and international aisles are next to each other in the middle — collect tahini, miso, gochujang and dried chiles in one pass rather than doubling back.

meijer.name: Meijer
meijer.note: A supercenter, so groceries are only half the building — enter on the grocery side or you will cross the whole store. Frozen runs along one long wall, which makes it worth saving for last.

aldi.name: Aldi
aldi.note: Single-loop store, so the aisle order barely matters. Great on frozen vegetables, olive oil, nuts, and canned beans; thinner on fresh herbs and specialty pantry items.

acme-fresh.name: Acme Fresh Market
acme-fresh.note: Strong local produce program in summer — Ohio sweet corn, tomatoes, and peaches in season.

farmers-market.name: Farmers market run
farmers-market.note: Seasonal, roughly late spring to autumn in most of the country. Buy produce, herbs and eggs here first, then fill the gaps at the store.
